# Dialogue Graph Editor - Complete User Guide
## Overview The Dialogue Graph Editor is a comprehensive visual editor for creating and managing dialogue systems in your game. It provides a split-view interface with a visual canvas on the left and a properties panel on the right.
## Getting Started
### Opening the Editor 1. In Unity, go to **Tools → Dialogue System → Open Graph Editor** 2. A window titled "Dialogue Graph Editor" will open
### Creating a New Dialogue Graph 1. Click the **New Graph** button in the toolbar 2. Choose a location and name for your dialogue graph file 3. The graph will be created and automatically loaded
### Loading an Existing Dialogue Graph 1. In the toolbar, use the object field labeled with the folder icon 2. Select a previously created DialogueGraph asset 3. The graph will load immediately
## Canvas Navigation
### Panning - **Middle Mouse Button** + Drag: Pan the view - **Alt + Left Click** + Drag: Alternative pan method
### Zooming - **Scroll Wheel**: Zoom in/out (0.3x to 3x magnification)
### Selecting Nodes - **Left Click** on a node: Select it (highlighted in green) - **Left Click** on empty space: Deselect all nodes
## Working with Nodes
### Creating Nodes 1. **Line Node**: Click "Add Line Node" in the toolbar - Represents a single line of dialogue spoken by a character - Can have conditions, commands, and lead to other nodes
2. **Choice Node**: Click "Add Choice Node" in the toolbar - Presents multiple options to the player - Each option can have different conditions and lead to different nodes
### Deleting Nodes 1. Select the node by clicking it 2. Either: - Click "Delete Selected" in the toolbar - Press the **Delete** key
> **⚠️ Warning**: Deleting a node will automatically remove all connections to it from other nodes.
### Connecting Nodes 1. Click the **→ (arrow button)** on the right edge of a node 2. Drag to the target node and release 3. A connection will be created from the source node to the target
To remove a connection, edit the target node's ID in the "Connections" section of the properties panel.
## Editing Node Properties
### The Properties Panel The right side of the editor displays all editable properties. When a node is selected, you can edit:
### Line Node Properties
**Basic Settings:** - **Text Key**: Integer ID for the dialogue text (used with localization system) - **Speaker ID**: Integer ID of the character speaking (-1 = None) - **Style ID**: Integer ID for text styling (0 = Default)
**Commands:** - **Add Command**: Adds an action that executes when this line plays - **Action ID**: Identifier for the command action - **Data**: Custom data string passed to the command - Delete individual commands with the **✕** button
**Conditions:** - **Add Condition**: Restricts when this line can be played - Store condition references as strings - Delete conditions with the **✕** button
### Choice Node Properties
**Options:** - **Add Option**: Creates a new selectable choice - For each option, configure: - **Text Key**: ID for the choice's display text - **Next Node**: ID of the node to jump to when selected - **Conditions**: Optional conditions that determine if this choice is available - Delete options with the **✕** button
### Common Properties
**Connections:** - **Next Nodes**: Lists all nodes that this node can lead to - Edit node IDs directly or remove specific connections - Visual connections are shown as bezier curves on the canvas
## Graph Properties
At the top of the properties panel, configure: - **Graph Name**: Display name for your dialogue - **Start Node**: ID of the first node to play when this graph is executed
## Saving Your Work
1. Make all your edits in the canvas and properties panel 2. Click the **Save** button in the toolbar 3. The graph will be saved to the project
> ** Tip**: Save frequently to avoid losing work!
## Workflow Tips
### Building a Simple Dialogue Tree 1. Create a Line Node to introduce the dialogue 2. Add a Choice Node with 2-3 options 3. Connect each option to different Line Nodes 4. For more branching, add more Choice Nodes 5. Connect endings to a final Line Node or back to earlier nodes
### Using Text Keys - Text Keys (integers) reference actual dialogue text in a localization system - Different Text Keys should map to different dialogue strings - This separation allows for multi-language support
### Using Speaker IDs - Speaker IDs identify which character is speaking - Typically: 0 = Player, 1+ = NPCs - Your game engine uses these IDs to determine voice lines and character portraits
### Advanced: Commands and Conditions - **Commands**: Execute actions like animations, sound effects, or game logic - Action ID maps to a command factory function - Custom Data allows you to pass parameters to commands
- **Conditions**: Control dialogue flow based on game state - Store serialized condition references - Your runtime system evaluates these to show/hide choices
## Common Issues and Solutions
**Q: Nodes aren't saving positions** - Node positions are recalculated each session for organization. This is by design.
**Q: Connections disappeared after editing** - Always save after making changes. Check the "Connections" section to verify links.
**Q: I can't see all my properties** - Scroll down in the properties panel to see more options.
**Q: How do I remove a connection?** - Go to the target node's properties and delete its entry from "Connections" → "Next Nodes"
## Integration with Runtime
Once you've created your dialogue graphs, they're used by: - **DialogueEngine**: Plays the dialogue graph - **IDialoguePresenter**: Displays dialogue and choices to the player - **Context/State System**: Evaluates conditions and executes commands
Connect your nodes' IDs and references to your game's localization, character, and action systems.
---
**Version**: 1.0 **Last Updated**: March 2026

# Dialogue Graph Editor - Example Workflows
## Example 1: Simple NPC Greeting
This example shows how to create a simple greeting dialogue.
### Steps: 1. **Create a new graph** called "NPC_Greeting" - Set Graph Name: "Greetings" - Set Start Node: 0
2. **Add Line Node** (ID: 0) - Text Key: 100 (greeting text) - Speaker ID: 1 (NPC) - Style ID: 0 (normal) - No commands or conditions
3. **Result**: When the graph plays, it shows the greeting and auto-advances
---
## Example 2: Simple Two-Choice Dialogue
Create a dialogue where the player chooses between accepting or declining a quest.
### Setup: 1. **Create graph** "NPC_QuestOffer" - Start Node: 0
2. **Add Line Node** (ID: 0) - Text Key: 101 ("Would you accept this quest?") - Speaker ID: 1 (NPC) - No commands/conditions - Connect to Node: 1
3. **Add Choice Node** (ID: 1) - **Option 0:** - Text Key: 102 ("Yes, I accept") - Next Node: 2 (acceptance response) - **Option 1:** - Text Key: 103 ("No thanks") - Next Node: 3 (decline response)
4. **Add Line Node** (ID: 2) - Text Key: 104 ("Great! Here's your quest.") - Speaker ID: 1 - Add Command: - Action ID: 5 (custom action for quest activation) - Data: "quest_id=42"
5. **Add Line Node** (ID: 3) - Text Key: 105 ("Come back if you change your mind.") - Speaker ID: 1
### Result: ``` Line 0: "Would you accept this quest?" ↓ Choice 1: Yes / No ↙ ↘ Line 2 Line 3 (Accept) (Decline) ```
---
## Example 3: Conditional Dialogue (Using Conditions)
Show different dialogue based on whether the player has a specific item.
### Setup: 1. **Create graph** "NPC_ConditionalDialogue"
2. **Add Line Node** (ID: 0) - Text Key: 200 ("Hello adventurer!") - Speaker ID: 1 - Next Node: 1
3. **Add Choice Node** (ID: 1) - **Option 0:** - Text Key: 201 ("I have the artifact you wanted") - Next Node: 2 - Condition: "player.HasItem(artifact_id)" → shows only if true - **Option 1:** - Text Key: 202 ("I don't have it yet") - Next Node: 3
4. **Add Line Node** (ID: 2) - Text Key: 203 ("Excellent! You've found it!") - Speaker ID: 1 - Commands: - Action ID: 10 (reward player) - Data: "reward_amount=500"
5. **Add Line Node** (ID: 3) - Text Key: 204 ("Please find it for me.") - Speaker ID: 1
### Result: ``` The choice in Node 1 to accept the artifact only appears if the condition "player.HasItem(artifact_id)" evaluates to true. ```
---
## Example 4: Multi-Turn Dialogue with Commands
A dialogue that plays animations and sounds.
### Setup: 1. **Create graph** "NPC_DramaticEncounter"
2. **Add Line Node** (ID: 0) - Text Key: 300 ("You dare challenge me?!") - Speaker ID: 5 (villain) - Commands: - Action ID: 1 (play animation) - Data: "animation=Villain_Taunt"
3. **Add Line Node** (ID: 1) - Text Key: 301 ("Feel the power of darkness!") - Speaker ID: 5 - Commands: - Action ID: 2 (play sound) - Data: "sound=evil_laugh.wav,volume=0.8" - (Add another command) - Action ID: 3 (effect) - Data: "effect=dark_aura"
4. **Add Choice Node** (ID: 2) - **Option 0:** - Text Key: 302 ("I won't back down!") - Next Node: 3 (fight) - **Option 1:** - Text Key: 303 ("I must flee!") - Next Node: 4 (escape)
### Result: ``` Dialogue plays with animations and sound effects creating an immersive dramatic encounter. ```
---
## Example 5: Branching Reputation System
Different dialogue endings based on reputation conditions.
### Setup: 1. **Create graph** "Merchant_Negotiation"
2. **Add Line Node** (ID: 0) - Text Key: 400 ("Welcome to my shop!") - Speaker ID: 2 (merchant)
3. **Add Choice Node** (ID: 1) - **Option 0:** - Text Key: 401 ("Give me a discount") - Next Node: 2 - (Both options lead to choice node 2)
4. **Add Choice Node** (ID: 2) - Response to discount request - **Option 0:** - Text Key: 402 ("Sure! Best friends get 20% off") - Next Node: 3 (accepted) - Condition: "merchant.reputation > 80" - **Option 1:** - Text Key: 403 ("Sorry, can't do that") - Next Node: 4 (rejected) - Condition: "merchant.reputation <= 80"
5. **Add Line Node** (ID: 3) - Text Key: 404 ("Here's your special price!") - Speaker ID: 2 - Commands: - Action ID: 8 (apply discount) - Data: "discount=0.2"
6. **Add Line Node** (ID: 4) - Text Key: 405 ("Full price or nothing.") - Speaker ID: 2
### Result: ``` Merchant gives discount only if reputation > 80, otherwise refuses. Use conditions to branch dialogue! ```
---
## Tips for Complex Dialogues
### Organization: - Use node IDs sequentially (0, 1, 2, 3...) - Group related nodes together in your mental model - Start with a simple flow, then add branching
### Testing: - Build one dialogue path completely first - Then add branches - Verify all connections before saving
### Text Keys: - Use consistent numbering (100s for greetings, 200s for shops, etc.) - Document what each key represents - Keep your localization system synchronized
### Conditions: - Start simple: "has_item", "reputation > X" - Progress to complex: "time_of_day == morning AND has_quest" - Your runtime system handles evaluation
### Commands: - Use meaningful Action IDs - Document what each ID does - Pass parameters through Data field
---
## Keyboard Shortcuts
- **Delete**: Delete selected node - **Middle Mouse + Drag** or **Alt + Left Click + Drag**: Pan canvas - **Scroll Wheel**: Zoom in/out - **Left Click**: Select node - **Left Click + Drag (on →)**: Create connection
---
## Common Patterns
### Linear Dialogue ``` Line 0 → Line 1 → Line 2 → Line 3 ```
### Simple Choice ``` Line 0 → Choice 1 → Line 2 (Yes) ↘ Line 3 (No) ```
### Nested Choices ``` Choice 1 → Choice 2 → Line A / Line B ↘ Line C ```
### Loop Back ``` Choice 1 → Line 2 ↑ ↓ └────────┘ (Player can ask again) ```
### Conditional Branch ``` Line 0 → Choice 1 → Line 2 (if condition) ↘ Line 3 (else) ```
---
**Start simple, build complexity gradually, and test as you go!**

**Root Cause:** The properties panel was using a broken hybrid of `GUI.ScrollViewScope` with manual absolute positioning (`Rect` calculations). This doesn't work in Unity's EditorGUILayout system.
**Solution:** - Converted all property drawing to use `EditorGUILayout` instead of manual Rect positioning - Created `DrawPropertiesPanelContent()` method with proper scroll view handling - All property editors now use automatic layout (`EditorGUILayout.TextField`, `EditorGUILayout.IntField`, etc.) - Added proper scope management with `EditorGUILayout.VerticalScope`

**Root Cause:** Coordinate space mismatch between: - Event handling (screen space mouse position) - Canvas drawing (local canvas space with pan/zoom) - Node rectangle calculations
**Solution:** - Stored `_currentCanvasArea` as a class variable to maintain consistent coordinate system - Updated `GetNodeRect()` to calculate positions in canvas-local space (not screen space) - Fixed `HandleCanvasEvents()` to convert mouse position from screen space to canvas space: `canvasMousePos = evt.mousePosition - area.position` - Now hit testing works correctly with zoom and pan applied

# Quick Start: Dialogue Graph Editor
## 30-Second Setup
1. **Open** Tools → Dialogue System → Open Graph Editor 2. **Create** a new graph or load existing one 3. **Add nodes** using "Add Line Node" and "Add Choice Node" buttons 4. **Click nodes** to select and edit in the properties panel 5. **Connect** by clicking the → button and dragging to another node 6. **Save** when done
Done! Your dialogue is ready.
---
## One-Minute Tutorial
### Create a Simple Dialogue
**Step 1: Create Graph** - Click "New Graph" - Save it as "MyDialogue"
**Step 2: Add First Line** - Click "Add Line Node" - Select it (turns green) - In Properties Panel, set: - Text Key: `1` - Speaker ID: `1`
**Step 3: Add Choice** - Click "Add Choice Node" - Select it - Click "Add Option" twice - Set Option 0: - Text Key: `10` - Next Node: `2` (add a node for this) - Set Option 1: - Text Key: `11` - Next Node: `3` (add a node for this)
**Step 4: Add Response Nodes** - Click "Add Line Node" (becomes node 2) - Text Key: `20` - Click "Add Line Node" (becomes node 3) - Text Key: `21`
**Step 5: Connect** - Click → on node 0 (Line) - Click node 1 (Choice) - Now node 0 connects to node 1
**Step 6: Save** - Click "Save"
**Done!** You have a working dialogue tree with branching choices.
---
## Property Panel Quick Reference
### When Selecting a Line Node:
**Required:** - **Text Key** - Number ID for dialogue text
**Optional:** - **Speaker ID** - Who's talking (0=player, 1+=NPC) - **Style ID** - How text appears (0=default)
**Advanced:** - **Commands** - Actions to execute (button: "Add Command") - Action ID: What to do (0-100+) - Data: Parameters for the action - **Conditions** - When line appears (button: "Add Condition") - Store condition string here
### When Selecting a Choice Node:
**Options List:** - Click "Add Option" for each choice - For each: - **Text Key** - What player sees - **Next Node** - Where it leads (node ID) - **Conditions** - Optional: when available
### For Any Node:
**Connections:** - **Next Nodes** - List of nodes this leads to - Edit node IDs directly - Delete connections with ✕
---
## Visual Indicators
- **Blue node** = Line Node (dialogue line) - **Orange node** = Choice Node (player picks) - **Green node** = Currently selected node - **Arrows (→)** = Connections between nodes
---
## Text Keys Explained
Text Keys are just numbers that your game uses to find the actual dialogue text.
**Example:** ``` Text Key 1 → "Hello adventurer!" Text Key 2 → "Would you help me?" Text Key 3 → "Yes, I'll help" Text Key 4 → "No, sorry" ```
You link these up in your localization/text system. The editor just stores the numbers.
---
## Speaker IDs Explained
Speaker IDs identify characters:
``` Speaker ID -1 = None (narrator) Speaker ID 0 = Player character Speaker ID 1 = First NPC (guard, merchant, etc) Speaker ID 2 = Second NPC (different character) Speaker ID 3+ = More characters ```
Your game's UI uses these to show character portraits and voices.
---
